headline: Low interaction risk: no shared channels or write surfaces, but ComfyUI’s file-backed inputs could still be misused if manually bridged into Dagster workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem read/write surfaces exposed here, and Dagster likewise has no shared channel with it. With no documented bridge, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between the pair.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI output into Dagster task definitions or metadata, injection risk appears.
IF a shared queue or file bridge is added later, re-evaluate the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from copy-paste workflows.
Do not route model outputs into Dagster config text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows filesystem read/write, clipboard, or network egress that would move shared data between them by default. ComfyUI touches local model assets, while Dagster lists no data classes or file surfaces, so there is no documented leakage path in this pair.
conditions: IF Dagster is configured to ingest ComfyUI artifacts from a shared directory, leakage risk becomes possible.
IF either agent is later given file-read or upload permissions, reassess.
mitigations: Keep model assets and pipeline assets in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets in ComfyUI workflow files.
Review any future file-sharing integration before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents lack filesystem write, git mutation, subprocess spawning, and OAuth scopes, so they cannot contend over shared mutable resources in the documented profiles. Dagster is also non-runnable here, further reducing conflict pathways.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory later, conflict risk changes.
IF Dagster is deployed with external orchestration that adds locks or writes, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in this deployment.
Do not share mutable working directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can orchestrate workflows, but this profile shows no direct input channel from ComfyUI and no evidence that Dagster treats ComfyUI output as authoritative by default. Any cascade would require an operator-created bridge, so the pathway exists only unusually and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are manually promoted into Dagster assets without validation, downstream errors can cascade.
IF a Dagster job is configured to trust generated artifacts as facts, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a human review step before Dagster consumes generated artifacts.
Label ComfyUI outputs as untrusted in pipeline metadata.
Use checksum or schema checks on imported artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent, and neither profile shows sensitive data classes or external transmission. With only docs-level evidence, there is no compliance breach pathway specific to this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into either agent, compliance must be rechecked.
IF deployment policies differ from the profiles, the assessment may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair by default.
Document any future retention or residency requirements before integration.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
